LESSON: CONSERVING FOOD NUTRIENTS • WASHING, PEELING, CUTTING, COOKING TIME, AND COVERING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Conserving food nutrients • Washing, peeling, cutting, cooking time, and covering
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 9

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Conserving food nutrients • Washing, peeling, cutting, cooking time, and covering, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How do we conserve vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables? 2.Why do we conserve vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Conserving food nutrients • Washing, peeling, cutting, cooking time, and covering together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: The learner develops skills on connecting using technology as they use digital devices to watch captioned video clips on

ways of conserving vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables

Values:
Respect: As a learner shows patience while discussing ways of conserving vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables in pairs.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Safety and security: The learner observes safety and security at home when using sharp kitchen tools and equipment to cut and peel

vegetables.

• Disaster Risk Reduction: The learner observes safety to prevent fire disaster in the kitchen while using fire to boil and cook.

Link to other learning areas:

Learners relate conservation of food nutrients to healthy growth and development learnt in integrated science.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Digital devices.

• Print reference materials such as recipe books.

• Cooking tools, equipment and materials.
